main.title: CMU 15-445/645: Intro to Database Systems
main.why: Storage, indexes, query execution and optimization, concurrency control and recovery. In English.

main.title: Architecture of a Database System
main.why: How real databases handle processes, memory and parallelism, which textbooks skip.

main.title: Are You Sure You Want to Use MMAP in Your Database Management System?
main.why: mmap looks like a free buffer pool, but letting the OS manage pages breaks transaction safety and stalls threads.

main.title: Evolution of Development Priorities in Key-value Stores Serving Large-scale Applications: The RocksDB Experience
main.why: RocksDB's priorities shifted from write amplification to space to CPU as its hardware and workloads changed.
InnoDB's B+tree wasted space and flash writes, so Facebook swapped it for RocksDB's LSM tree under MySQL.

main.title: The Part of PostgreSQL We Hate the Most
main.why: Postgres MVCC copies the whole row on each update, causing bloat and vacuum pain.

further.title: Yes, PostgreSQL Has Problems. But We're Sticking With It!

main.title: An Overview of Query Optimization in Relational Systems
main.why: SQL leaves the plan to the system, and this survey explains how optimizers search and cost plans, starting from System R.

main.title: How Good Are Query Optimizers, Really?
main.why: Cardinality estimates are often far off and matter more than the cost model, as the Join Order Benchmark shows.

main.title: A Critique of ANSI SQL Isolation Levels
main.why: The ANSI isolation levels are defined too vaguely, and the paper adds snapshot isolation, which still allows write skew.

main.title: Serializable Isolation for Snapshot Databases
main.why: Snapshot isolation still allows write skew, so SSI detects dangerous patterns at runtime and aborts a transaction, as PostgreSQL does.
Too many concurrent transactions lowered throughput, and a smaller connection pool fixed it.

main.title: C-Store: A Column-oriented DBMS
main.why: Analytic queries read a few columns of many rows, so C-Store stores data by column and reads only what a query needs.

main.title: MonetDB/X100: Hyper-Pipelining Query Execution
main.why: Row-at-a-time execution wastes CPU on interpretation, so X100's vectorized operators process a batch of values per call.

main.title: DuckDB: an Embeddable Analytical Database
main.why: Analysts needed fast analytics inside their own process, so DuckDB is embedded like SQLite but columnar and vectorized.

main.title: What Goes Around Comes Around... And Around...
main.why: Many data models tried to replace SQL, and this retrospective shows how SQL and the relational model absorbed their best ideas.
Altering a busy MySQL table can block writes, so online migration tools copy it to a shadow table in the background and swap it in.
GitHub upgraded its whole MySQL fleet in stages, replicas first, while replicating back to the old version so it could roll back.
Postgres uses one process per connection, so Figma built a pooler that sheds load.
Clients connecting straight to ZippyDB hosts formed a fragile many-to-many mesh, so a proxy tier now bounds connections and batches requests across clients.
VIP and DNS based failover was slow and fragile, so GitHub uses orchestrator to promote a replica and Consul with GLB to route clients to it.
Notion's single Postgres was nearing its limits, so it split the data into logical shards by workspace and migrated with double writes.
